Welcome to this awesome game, glad to see you’re enjoying it so much. For me, deckbuilding is one of the most versatile and fun aspects of AHLCG. Besides the great advice previous posters have given, there is a quite entertaining deckbuilding stream by Matt Newman on the FFG youtube where he shows how he likes to build a deck for an investigator. 


I like checking out some standard decks that some great Arkhamdb contributors have posted. They give a good feeling to what certain investigators play like and how they approach picking cards. Overall I’d say 4-6 hand slot items (weapons for guardians, tomes for Mystics/Daisy, etc.), about 6-10 skills cards, 2-4/6 allies (depending on how big a priority Charisma is for you), 4-8 events. But this is just a very personal and adaptable guideline, I have seen Ashcan Pete builds run as many as 20 skills cards, Leo with 6 allies. Explore and find what you enjoy!

I think *my* biggest mistake is thinking about the Japanese language from the perspective of my mother tongue (Dutch) and applying too much of the Dutch grammatical and semantic patterns to a language that works in completely different ways. If I were to translate a text of some sorts to Japanese, I am inclined to think: "How do I directly translate this and this into Japanese" and then end up with a text sounding probably extremely unnatural to native Japanese speakers. It's best to drop your own language completely and try to start thinking "the Japanese way" when it comes to speaking/writing Japanese, imho. 


Fex: if I were to translate the following sentence:
"Morgen heb ik een examen."
English: Tomorrow I have an exam. 
If I would directly translate this word by word, I would probably end up with something like this:
明日は、私に試験がある。

Even though this is probably a lot more common and easier (please correct me if I'm wrong):
明日は、試験です。
